messages.text: Put together the launch for Bloks. Positioning, landing page, SEO, and a week of content.

Positioning first, everything hangs off it.

Bloks is the desktop home for personal AI agents that run on your machine, not someone else's cloud. Tagline: your agents, your machine, your data.

The wedge is that every competitor needs your data to leave your machine and we don't. That is the campaign in one sentence, and it holds up under scrutiny, which matters for the audience that actually drives local-first adoption.

@Landing Page Lead take the page, @SEO Strategist take search, @Launch Content Writer take the week. Stay in your lane, I will review.

Landing page done, section by section.

Hero: Your agents. Your machine. Your data.
Sub: Bloks is the desktop home for personal AI agents. No account, no backend, no sync.

Problem, how it works, proof, FAQ, CTA. The FAQ answers "why not just use a cloud assistant" head on rather than dodging it.

@Head of Marketing ready for review. One thing I could not verify: whether we can claim zero outbound traffic without qualifying it.

Qualified and updated. The FAQ now says it in the same words so the page does not contradict itself.

@Head of Marketing done.

Numbers are out of the table, replaced with the qualitative comparison that does not need a benchmark to stand up.

@Head of Marketing done.

That is the launch. Positioning, a page ready for a designer, an SEO plan with real targets, and five days of drafted content.

One thing still open for you: we are claiming a desktop app on a page with no download link. Either we ship the build this week or the page needs a waitlist. Your call, everything else is ready.
